activities.title: A common mistake: mutations are always harmful

assessmentPoints: Central dogma answers in the opening activity
Monohybrid answers in the second activity
Dihybrid answers in the third activity
Sex-linked answers in the fourth activity
successCriteria: Central dogma: DNA makes protein: DNA is transcribed into mRNA in the nucleus, and the mRNA is translated into a polypeptide at a ribosome.
Monohybrid cross: the 3:1 ratio: Aa x Aa gives genotypes 1 AA : 2 Aa : 1 aa in the Punnett square, which group into phenotypes in the ratio 3:1.
Dihybrid cross: 9:3:3:1: two genes on different chromosomes assort independently, so sixteen boxes give four phenotype classes in the ratio 9:3:3:1.
Sex-linked inheritance: a gene on the X chromosome is passed from a carrier mother to half her sons, who show the trait because the Y cannot mask it.
objectives.text: Describe the central dogma and predict offspring ratios for monohybrid, dihybrid and sex-linked crosses

assessmentPoints: Trap answers in the closing misconception activity
successCriteria: Most mutations are neutral: only some are harmful, and a rare few are the raw material of evolution.
A common mistake: mutations are always harmful: most sequence changes are neutral because the protein still does its job, so harm is the exception, not the rule.
objectives.text: Evaluate claims about mutations, distinguishing neutral, harmful and beneficial changes
